description:
Create a new provider version

Creates a new immutable semantic version of a provider. Every recipe change needs its own version; existing versions are never edited in place. Defaults to a patch bump. Publish it with publish_provider_version, or submit it for review with submit_provider_version_for_review.

body.description: Body for creating a new version of a provider. Every new version starts on the `draft` branch — see `CreateProviderVersion`. The request body never sets `branch` directly; going live is a separate, explicit step (publish for PRIVATE, submit-for-review → approve for PUBLIC). `verificationType` defaults to `structured`; pass `llm` with a `prompt` to author an AI-verification provider.

items.description: A template for selecting requests. Same matcher shape as `RequestSelection`, plus template flags (`multiple`/`required`) and optional `templateParams` expansion.

additionalClientOptions.description: Apply TLS configuration when creating the tunnel to the attestor.

supportedProtocolVersions.description: TLS protocol versions the client is allowed to negotiate.

credentials.description: Mirrors the Fetch API `RequestCredentials` value used when issuing the request — controls whether cookies and auth headers are sent.

headers.description: Static HTTP request headers passed to the attestor. Values may contain `{{param}}` and `{{context.key}}` templates.

method.description: The HTTP method used for the request.

multiple.description: If true, the template is allowed for multiple requests. Useful for requests like paginated API calls.

requestBodyTemplate.description: Template used to match or capture an outgoing request body. Template can use regex templates as placeholders. For example, to match an outgoing request body that contains a request ID, you can use the following template: `(?<requestId>.*)`.

required.description: If true, a request is required to match with this template. If not requests matches this template in proof, then validation fails.

responseMatches.description: Conditions the (redacted) response must satisfy for the proof to be valid. Each runs against the union of the portions revealed by `responseRedactions` (or the whole response when there are none). Mirrors attestor-core `responseMatches`.

items.description: Specifies a rule to match against a string in response to validate proof content.

description.description: The description of the field that is extracted using this match rule

isOptional.description: If true, the match condition is optional and won't fail if absent

order.description: The order in which the field should be displayed to user in UI

type.description: The matching mechanism to use value as against response. Typically regex or simple string containment

value.description: The pattern or value to look for in the response. When `type` is 'contains', supports template variable declaration using `{{variable}}` syntax. When `type` is 'regex', can be used to extract variables using regex named groups.

responseRedactions.description: Portions to select/reveal from the response, applied in order (xPath => jsonPath => regex). Done client-side; only the selected portions (plus the first response line) are sent to the attestor. An independent ordered list — not generally paired 1:1 with `responseMatches`. For legacy proof-hash optional-subset compatibility only, the redaction at the same index is treated as the pair for an optional `ResponseMatch`; this does not pair all redactions with matches. Mirrors attestor-core `responseRedactions`.

items.description: Which portions to select from a response. These are selected in order, xpath => jsonPath => regex * These redactions are done client side and only the selected portions are sent to the attestor. The attestor will only be able to see the selected portions alongside the first line of the HTTP response (that is, "HTTP/1.1 200 OK")

hash.description:
If provided, the value inside will be hashed instead of being redacted. Useful for cases where the data inside is an identifiying piece of information that you don't want to reveal to the attestor, eg. an email address.
If the hash function produces more bytes than the original value, the hash will be truncated.
Eg. if hash is enabled, the original value is "hello", and hashed is "a1b2c", then the attestor will only see "a1b2c".
Note: if a regex with named groups is provided, only the named groups will be hashed.

jsonPath.description: expect a JSON response, retrieve the item at this path using dot notation, for example 'email.addresses.0'.

regex.description: select a regex match from the response

xPath.description: expect an HTML response, and to contain a certain xpath for eg. "/html/body/div.a1/div.a2/span.a5"

templateParams.description: Names of `${param}` placeholders used in this template's `responseMatches` / `responseRedactions`, substituted at verification time from array-valued extracted parameters (each name must resolve to an array of values; all named arrays must have the same length). Absent or empty means the template is used as-is with no expansion.

templateParamsMode.description: How array values of `templateParams` expand the template: `separate` (default) emits one expanded request — its own claim — per value; `merge` emits a single request whose `responseMatches`/`responseRedactions` contain all substituted entries, proven by one claim.

url.description: The URL or generic path of the HTTP request.

writeRedactionMode.description:
How the matched portion of the response should be redacted before the transcript is handed to the attestor.
- `zk`: redact using a zero-knowledge proof over the original
  bytes.

- `key-update`: redact by performing a TLS key update so the
  attestor never observes the matched bytes in cleartext.

prompt.description: Extraction prompt, used (and required) when `verificationType` is `llm`. Gated by the prompt guard before it is stored (docs/prompt-guard.md).

items.description: A matcher for one HTTP request in observed traffic, together with the response constraints that must hold for a Reclaim proof over that request to be valid. Used by interceptors, in-page injections, and LLM agents.

requiredContext.description: Optional JSON Schema describing the `context` a Consumer must supply when creating a verification session for this provider version. Only needed when the recipe expects Consumer-supplied values: those are referenced as `{{context.<key>}}` in recipe requests. Bare `{{parameterName}}` placeholders are normally provider parameters extracted from claimant traffic. For old DevTools recipes, Builder-mode Verification Clients seed a missing bare `parameterName` from a same-named scalar session context field when the recipe doesn't use `{{context.parameterName}}`; an explicit parameter always wins. New recipes should use the explicit `{{context.<key>}}` form. Bare parameters need no declaration here. Builder-owned `reclaimSessionId` and `attestationNonce` remain context-only. The Builder validates `CreateVerificationSessionRequest.context` against this schema and rejects the request (400) on mismatch. Extra context fields are always allowed regardless of the schema (a root-level `additionalProperties: false` is ignored). Empty/absent accepts any context.

verificationType.description: How a provider version verifies a claim. `structured` uses the explicit match rules on this version (the `matches` / `allowedJsMatches` and related settings). `llm` defers the verification decision to a language model and requires `prompt` to be set.

branch.description:
Branch (lifecycle stage) of this provider version.

- `ai`: changes authored by the AI assistant live on this branch.

- `draft`: a human is actively editing the version.

- `fixed`: a proven AI repair. It remains pinned to its explicit
  version and does not replace the live trunk version.

- `in_review`: the author has submitted the version to be made
  public and it is awaiting review. On approval the branch tag
  is cleared (the version is promoted to the live channel and becomes
  public).

- `rejected`: review concluded with a rejection. When the author
  addresses the feedback the branch transitions back to
  `in_review`.

buildNumber.description: Build number for the provider version

webSettings.description: Settings used by the web-based verification client.

browserRequestActions.description: Portal-only authenticated browser actions available to `jsUserScripts` through `window.Reclaim.browserRequest`.

items.description: A portal-only, provider-declared HTTP action for `window.Reclaim.browserRequest`. The claimant page supplies only the action id and declared primitive inputs; the recipe controls the HTTPS origin, request template, and returned fields. Other Verification Clients currently ignore this field.

bodyTemplate.description: JSON template whose `{{name}}` inputs are inserted as JSON literals. The rendered body is limited again at execution time.

cookieValueHeader.description: Copies one same-origin, script-readable cookie into a request header. The cookie value stays inside the verification client's browser.

headersTemplate.description: Header values may interpolate declared `{{name}}` inputs.

includeBody.description: Return the bounded raw response body.

omitOriginHeader.description: Remove Chromium's automatic Origin header from a fetch action. Unsupported for navigate actions.

pathTemplate.description: Optional origin-relative path/query template. Declared inputs use `{{name}}` and are URL-encoded.

transport.description: `fetch` is the default. `navigate` supports GET only and performs a top-level navigation in the action's isolated browser page.

userAgent.description: Browser User-Agent applied to the isolated action page before its first navigation. Use only when the target origin requires a specific browser identity.

clientOptions.description: Options that influence how the web verification client behaves.

extension.description: Free-form key-value configuration for the browser-extension verification client. Keys and value shapes are defined by the extension client; values may be any JSON. Absent by default.

inapp.description: Options that influence how the in-app verification client behaves.

interceptorSettings.description: Free-form configuration passed through to the interceptor implementation selected by `interceptorType`. Keys and value shapes are defined by the chosen interceptor.

isDocumentRequestReplayEnabled.description: Whether the main document request is replayed via the attestor

android.description: User-agent string used for platform verification.

ios.description: User-agent string used for platform verification.

portal.description: Options that influence how the portal verification client behaves.

useProxy.description: When true, network traffic from the portal client and attestation is routed through a proxy.

userAgent.description: User-agent string used for platform verification.

geoLocation.description: Geographic location the verification should appear to originate from: a 2-letter ISO country code, or a parameter the attestor resolves at proof time. `{{DYNAMIC_GEO}}` and `{{DYNAMIC_GEO_SECRET}}` are the Verification Client's standard names for the end-user's own country — the `_SECRET` one is delivered as a secret param, so the attestor never learns which country the proof egressed from.

jsUserScripts.description: JavaScript snippets injected into the page which runs before every page load. `window.Reclaim.` APIs are available to these scripts to request actions to the client like claim creation.
